title: UPC Codebook
description: A named coding scheme: the controlled vocabulary of codes a coder may apply (§12). A codebook is the SCHEME; a coding is one JUDGEMENT that applies one of its codes to one target. Identity is over (namespace, slug) and NOT over codes[], because a controlled vocabulary's job is to stay stable while its contents evolve — hashing the code list would dangle every codebook_ref on every edit. Evolution is carried by the advisory revision / revision_digest pair instead.

namespace.description: The owning tool or project, e.g. "researchassistant". Namespacing is what lets two tools define an "org-type" codebook without collision.

slug.description: Stable machine name within the namespace, e.g. "org-type". Renaming the human title never changes identity; changing the slug mints a new codebook.

title.description: Human-readable name, shown in a browsing surface.

question.description: The question this codebook answers, e.g. "What kind of organization published this source?"

closed.description: true: a coding MUST carry a `code` drawn from codes[]. false: a coding MUST carry a free-text `value` instead (an open/emergent scheme). Enforced by coding_code_unknown / coding_open_closed_mismatch (§08).

multi_label.description: Whether one coder may apply more than one code from this codebook to the same target. Advisory: it informs a UI and the coding_disagreement advisory, and is never a hard error.

revision.description: Monotonic revision of codes[]. Advisory; deliberately NOT in the cbk- identity recipe and NOT in the cod- recipe, so editing a codebook never re-mints its codings.

revision_digest.description: "sha256:" + sha256(JCS(codes)). A coding records the revision it was made under; a mismatch raises the advisory coding_codebook_drift (§08), exactly as input_digest raises stale_input.

codes.description: The codes themselves. For an open codebook (closed:false) this MAY be a seed list that codings are not restricted to.

code.description: Stable machine token, used in the cod- identity recipe. Renaming `label` is free; changing `code` mints new codings.

definition.description: What this code means and when to apply it. §09 requires a browsing surface to make this reachable in one interaction — an undefined code is uninterpretable jargon.

parent.description: Another `code` in this same codebook, forming a hierarchy. Rollups are computed by a reader (the projection rule, §09) and MUST NOT be stored.

deprecated.description: Retained so existing codings stay resolvable, but not offered for new coding.

ext.description: Tool-private extension data, namespaced by tool.
